text: At the Ruvenna data centre last spring, a routine software update triggered the outage, according to records I reviewed and staff I spoke with on site. The failure hit at 2:17 a.m. on April 18, when technicians were pushing a patch to the facility’s power-management system. Within minutes, servers in three halls dropped offline, and backup controls failed to hand over cleanly. “The update didn’t like the older firmware,” maintenance supervisor Elena Voss told me, standing beside the darkened west wing. Power was restored by 6:40 a.m., but the interruption briefly affected 14 municipal clients and several local firms. One engineer called it “a classic update mistake, not a hardware collapse.”
